row = one classified pointer; quiet = min(stream silence, launch window)
quiet > window ?
the only stall decision, both surfaces
worker alive, live child under it
window = max(window, budget_seconds)
the child is the job, and the worker's own
silence says nothing about a job running
a short budget never narrows the window
process_descendant_alive is True
any other reading keeps 15m
worker dead · no live child · foreign host
descendant unknown (None, not False)
a live worker with nothing running beneath
it is the case a stall most often means hung
None is "nothing was asked", never an absence
one reading, taken beside the liveness read
/proc/<worker-pid>/task/<tid>/children → one level, then runs.process_alive(child)
pid asked is the worker record's where it names one: a supervisor holds its worker as a child, so the
pointer's pid would answer "a child lives" for every supervised run and make the narrowing vacuous
read only where this host took the liveness reading; a foreign pid is never asked
